title: Cenote Taj Mahal - Expédition Yuc 96
credits: Topo degré 3 (UIS), Yuc 96 (FMAS, FFS, FFESSM; French cave-diving expedition). North arrow: magnetic north 1996; 100 m scale bar
placementWhy: Moderate (about 20-25 m): free similarity fit on four points, residuals 24, 19, 5 and 5 m; 0.429 m/px (the 100 m scale bar says 0.400, 7% apart) and 2.3 degrees of rotation, close to the 1996 magnetic north. Ground points: Cenote Taj Mahal's pool on the database's Taj Mahal (Open Caves source, taken on site) and Mangrova on the centre of the ring-shaped pond on the satellite (the only open water; both used by the placed Gerrard 2001 and Yuc 97/98 maps). These two are only 210 m apart and the map's Taj - Mangrova bearing is 9 degrees off the ground's (a two-point fit turns the map 9 degrees and puts its far ends 100 m off), so the scale and rotation over the whole map are taken from the placed Yuc 97/98 map, which draws the same survey (its Taj Mahal part matches this plan passage for passage) and was fitted on five ground points over 1.6 km: its Vista Bonita pond and the NW tip of its Estrela collapse (this map's C9) are the other two points. As on the Yuc 97/98 map, the pool lands about 24 m N of the database's Taj Mahal point (on the sandy clearing S of it, as on the Gerrard map). The rest of the imagery is closed canopy (no other pond to check). Cross-checked: the traced walls run on the Yuc 97/98 walls within a few metres everywhere they both draw; the Gerrard 2001 map's Buena Vista lands 55 m from Vista Bonita, its Sacrado 71 m from Sagrada (C5), its Twin Cenotes 37 m from C6.

trace.why: b/w hand drawing (Yuc 96 style, like the Jaguar map): walls are bold smooth lines (4-6 px), passages white, boulders as small closed outlines, collapses hatched. The walls are smooth enough that the straight-line eraser took long runs of them: it is off (straightMinPx 2000) and the section lines A-G are erased by hand (eraseLines), leaving the pixels where they cross a wall. Sagrada's hatched collapse is a solid band: traced along its outer edge (outlineAreas). Mangrova's mangrove symbols (inside the pond) and the labels OCR misses are masked. keepEntranceInk: the entrance boxes would otherwise mask the C9 blob (a gap in the wall) and the section-C shaft.

entrances.name: Vista Bonita (Buena Vista)

entrances.name: unnamed shaft (section C)
entrances.why: small oval in the passage W of Taj Mahal where section C is cut; the section draws a narrow shaft from the surface into the water-filled passage. 48 m from the placed Gerrard 2001 map's Cenote Sugarbowl and Points of Light: possibly one of them (the database's Taj Mahal description: a 200 ft traverse from Taj Mahal to Sugarbowl through a room with three holes).

entrances.name: C5 Sagrada
entrances.why: The map's cenote C5, named Sagrada, at the NE end of a hatched collapse: the database's Sacrado ('Sacred', sistema Tajma Ha, no position). The placed Gerrard 2001 map's Cenote Sacrado lands 71 m S of it; the Yuc 97/98 map's small pool at the end of the passage SE of Taj Mahal 37 m.

entrances.name: C6
entrances.why: cenote at the end of the passage E of Sagrada; the Yuc 97/98 map's brown and orange pond pair 24 m away; the placed Gerrard 2001 map's Twin Cenotes 37 m - possibly the same.

entrances.name: C7
entrances.why: small cenote at a passage end, inside the SW lobe of the Yuc 97/98 map's Estrela collapse (Gerrard's City of Agre); not named.

symbols.why: French UIS plan (Yuc 96, same style as the Yuc 95/96 Jaguar and the Yuc 96 Aktun Koh maps): no legend, no depths (no overlined, underlined or minus-sign numbers anywhere on the plan), no letter codes, no water-flow arrows, no bones symbol or bones text (checked by eye over the whole plan and in the OCR words). The section box (A-G) shows water levels only. Kept: two short dashed arrows leaving the passage ends beyond C9 (the survey goes on unsurveyed / passage continues), as leads-to. Cenotes C5-C9 are entrances.
